youtube_title: The Kingsbury Ordnance Plant: the LaPorte County farms that became a World War 2 shell plant
body: In 1940, the Army picked the farmland around Kingsbury for a war plant, and the families who lived there had to leave. More than 13,000 acres of farms became the Kingsbury Ordnance Plant. It loaded shells and ammunition for World War 2, and at its peak more than 20,000 people worked there, nearly half of them women. A whole new town went up beside it: Victory City, today's Kingsford Heights. After the war and a second run for Korea, the plant shut down for good, but out in the woods, rows of old ammunition bunkers still stand. Part of the old plant is an industrial park now, and part is the Kingsbury Fish and Wildlife Area, open to the public (register at the kiosk).
